ai.description: *Ophisops kutchensis* reaches 5 cm snout-vent length. It is olive-brown with two distinct white dorsolateral stripes and possesses fused eyelids forming a transparent spectacle over the eyes.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ophisops kutchensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a single, undivided supraocular scale, whereas similar species in the region typically possess two.
ai.habitat: *Ophisops kutchensis* inhabits arid, open scrublands and rocky grasslands in the Indian subcontinent, typically found at low altitudes in semi-desert landscapes.
ai.behavior: *Ophisops kutchensis* is a diurnal lizard that actively forages for small insects by darting across open, arid ground during the warmest parts of the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ophisops kutchensis* is oviparous, laying clutches of 2–4 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ophisops kutchensis* is endemic to the arid regions of Gujarat, India, primarily inhabiting the Kutch district and surrounding semi-arid scrublands at low elevations.
